relevance_note: This 24-patient pediatric PID cohort includes one patient with a TNFAIP3 variant: 'Genetic analysis revealed a heterozygous c.259C>T mutation in TNFAIP3, indicating an A20 deficiency'.
method_note: Read the whole paper by hand; the JSON was assembled with a short Python script whose values and spans were typed from my reading, and every span was checked verbatim against the Markdown by script. Scope decision: only Patient #18 (the single TNFAIP3 carrier) is extracted. The other 23 patients have other PID diagnoses or non-TNFAIP3/non-diagnostic genetics (TTC37, BLM, RFXANK, SH2D1A, STXBP2, FOXP3, NBAS, NLRP1, TAZ/CFTR) and are not relatives of Patient #18, so they were left out of this HA20 extraction; no variants in other genes are recorded. Age 192 is Table 2 column 'A' (age at the time of diagnosis, months), recorded as age at diagnosis (P16Y = 192 months). Table 2 'Physical findings' and 'Additional manifestations' are '-' for #18 and were treated as not reported (rule 6). The authors give no protein change, transcript or variant class for c.259C>T; none was inferred. 'Lymphonodular hyperplasia' (intestinal histology) was recorded as an observed feature but NOT mapped to the checklist item 'lymphoproliferation or lymphadenopathy' (abstained). Hypogammaglobulinemia and bloody diarrhea have no checklist item. No patient-level fever, CRP/ESR, skin, joint or autoimmune data for #18. Group counts (Tables 1 and 4) were not used for exclusions. is_proband left null (cohort patient, not called proband). cites_prior_report left null (paper is silent). Contradictions/oddities in the paper (none concern Patient #18): Patient #9 appears in two Table 2 rows differing only in physical findings; Patient #17 gene is 'NLRP1' in text but 'NRP1' in Table 2; Patient #23 is listed as 'Sibling of patient #23'; Patient #12 WES is 'non-diagnostic' in Results but 'Whole exome sequencing was not performed' in Discussion; Table 2 is captioned n=19 but lists #9 twice.
